claim: A genetic variant in the gene PTPN22 (R620W, rs2476601) is strongly associated with increased risk for multiple autoimmune diseases.
source: A genetic variant in the gene PTPN22 (R620W, rs2476601) is strongly associated with increased risk for multiple autoimmune diseases and linked to altered TCR regulation and T cell activation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established background information about PTPN22 R620W.

claim: PTPN22 R620W is linked to altered TCR regulation and T cell activation.
source: A genetic variant in the gene PTPN22 (R620W, rs2476601) is strongly associated with increased risk for multiple autoimmune diseases and linked to altered TCR regulation and T cell activation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established background information.

claim: PTPN22 risk edited cells exhibited increased activation marker expression following non-specific TCR engagement.
source: PTPN22 risk edited cells exhibited increased activation marker expression following non-specific TCR engagement, findings that mimicked PTPN22 KO cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 2.

claim: PTPN22 risk edited cells mimicked PTPN22 KO cells in activation marker expression.
source: PTPN22 risk edited cells exhibited increased activation marker expression following non-specific TCR engagement, findings that mimicked PTPN22 KO cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 2.

claim: Loss of PTPN22 function led to enhanced signaling in T cells expressing a lower avidity self-reactive TCR.
source: Next, using lentiviral delivery of T1D patient-derived TCRs against the pancreatic autoantigen, islet-specific glucose-6 phosphatase catalytic subunit-related protein (IGRP), we demonstrate that loss of PTPN22 function led to enhanced signaling in T cells expressing a lower avidity self-reactive TCR, but not a high-avidity TCR.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Loss of PTPN22 function did not enhance signaling in T cells expressing a high-avidity TCR.
source: Next, using lentiviral delivery of T1D patient-derived TCRs against the pancreatic autoantigen, islet-specific glucose-6 phosphatase catalytic subunit-related protein (IGRP), we demonstrate that loss of PTPN22 function led to enhanced signaling in T cells expressing a lower avidity self-reactive TCR, but not a high-avidity TCR.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Loss of PTPN22 mediated enhanced proliferation in T cells expressing a lower avidity TCR.
source: In this setting, loss of PTPN22 mediated enhanced proliferation and Th1 skewing.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: Loss of PTPN22 mediated Th1 skewing in T cells expressing a lower avidity TCR.
source: In this setting, loss of PTPN22 mediated enhanced proliferation and Th1 skewing.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 5.

claim: Expression of the PTPN22 risk variant in association with a lower avidity TCR increased proliferation relative to PTPN22 non-risk T cells.
source: Importantly, expression of the risk variant in association with a lower avidity TCR also increased proliferation relative to PTPN22 non-risk T cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 6.

claim: PTPN22 rs2476601 contributes to autoimmunity risk by permitting increased TCR signaling and activation in mildly self-reactive T cells.
source: Together, these findings suggest that, in primary human T cells, PTPN22 rs2476601 contributes to autoimmunity risk by permitting increased TCR signaling and activation in mildly self-reactive T cells, thereby potentially expanding the self-reactive T cell pool and skewing this population toward an inflammatory phenotype.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings presented in the abstract.

claim: PTPN22 rs2476601 potentially expands the self-reactive T cell pool.
source: Together, these findings suggest that, in primary human T cells, PTPN22 rs2476601 contributes to autoimmunity risk by permitting increased TCR signaling and activation in mildly self-reactive T cells, thereby potentially expanding the self-reactive T cell pool and skewing this population toward an inflammatory phenotype.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings presented in the abstract.

claim: PTPN22 rs2476601 skews self-reactive T cells toward an inflammatory phenotype.
source: Together, these findings suggest that, in primary human T cells, PTPN22 rs2476601 contributes to autoimmunity risk by permitting increased TCR signaling and activation in mildly self-reactive T cells, thereby potentially expanding the self-reactive T cell pool and skewing this population toward an inflammatory phenotype.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings presented in the abstract.

claim: The greatest risk factor for most autoimmune disease is HLA haplotype.
source: While the greatest risk factor for most autoimmune disease is HLA haplotype (Todd et al., 2007; Bonifacio et al., 2018), an individual's total genetic risk is determined by a combination of gene variants (Sharma et al., 2018; Cotsapas et al., 2011), many of which cluster near genes responsible for regulating immune responses (Farh et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Todd et al., 2007 and Bonifacio et al., 2018.

claim: An individual's total genetic risk for autoimmune disease is determined by a combination of gene variants.
source: While the greatest risk factor for most autoimmune disease is HLA haplotype (Todd et al., 2007; Bonifacio et al., 2018), an individual's total genetic risk is determined by a combination of gene variants (Sharma et al., 2018; Cotsapas et al., 2011), many of which cluster near genes responsible for regulating immune responses (Farh et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sharma et al., 2018 and Cotsapas et al., 2011.

claim: Many autoimmune risk gene variants cluster near genes responsible for regulating immune responses.
source: While the greatest risk factor for most autoimmune disease is HLA haplotype (Todd et al., 2007; Bonifacio et al., 2018), an individual's total genetic risk is determined by a combination of gene variants (Sharma et al., 2018; Cotsapas et al., 2011), many of which cluster near genes responsible for regulating immune responses (Farh et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Farh et al., 2015.

claim: PTPN22 can function to modulate a range of immune signaling programs.
source: While the phosphatase encoded by PTPN22 can function to modulate a range of immune signaling programs, it has been best studied in lymphocyte antigen receptor regulation (Cohen et al., 1999; Wu et al., 2006; Hill et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cohen et al., 1999; Wu et al., 2006; Hill et al., 2002.

claim: PTPN22 has been best studied in lymphocyte antigen receptor regulation.
source: While the phosphatase encoded by PTPN22 can function to modulate a range of immune signaling programs, it has been best studied in lymphocyte antigen receptor regulation (Cohen et al., 1999; Wu et al., 2006; Hill et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cohen et al., 1999; Wu et al., 2006; Hill et al., 2002.

claim: PTPN22 R620W is broadly associated with a large number of autoimmune diseases.
source: An arginine to tryptophan substitution (R620W) resulting from a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP; rs2476601) within PTPN22 is broadly associated with a large number of autoimmune diseases (Zheng et al., 2012; Tizaoui et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Zheng et al., 2012 and Tizaoui et al., 2019.

claim: PTPN22 R620W is one of the strongest, non-HLA, genetic risk factors for autoimmune diseases.
source: PTPN22 R620W, hereafter referred to as the PTPN22 risk variant, is one of the strongest, non-HLA, genetic risk factors for autoimmune diseases, nearly doubling a carrier's risk of type 1 diabetes, systemic lupus erythematosus, or rheumatoid arthritis (Bottini et al., 2004; Begovich et al., 2004; Kyogoku et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bottini et al., 2004; Begovich et al., 2004; Kyogoku et al., 2004.

claim: PTPN22 R620W nearly doubles a carrier's risk of type 1 diabetes, systemic lupus erythematosus, or rheumatoid arthritis.
source: PTPN22 R620W, hereafter referred to as the PTPN22 risk variant, is one of the strongest, non-HLA, genetic risk factors for autoimmune diseases, nearly doubling a carrier's risk of type 1 diabetes, systemic lupus erythematosus, or rheumatoid arthritis (Bottini et al., 2004; Begovich et al., 2004; Kyogoku et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Bottini et al., 2004; Begovich et al., 2004; Kyogoku et al., 2004.

claim: In T cells, PTPN22 functions to dephosphorylate key activating tyrosine residues within LCK and ZAP70 in the TCR signaling pathway.
source: In T cells, PTPN22 functions to dephosphorylate key activating tyrosine residues within the proximal tyrosine kinase effectors, LCK and ZAP70, in the TCR signaling pathway (Wu et al., 2006; Bottini et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Wu et al., 2006 and Bottini et al., 2004.

claim: PTPN22 function is mediated in concert with activity through PTPN22's binding partner, C-terminal Src kinase (CSK).
source: This function is mediated in concert with activity through PTPN22's binding partner, C-terminal Src kinase (CSK), which also regulates LCK activity (Cloutier and Veillette, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cloutier and Veillette, 1999.

claim: CSK regulates LCK activity.
source: This function is mediated in concert with activity through PTPN22's binding partner, C-terminal Src kinase (CSK), which also regulates LCK activity (Cloutier and Veillette, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Cloutier and Veillette, 1999.

claim: Co-association of PTPN22 and CSK results in residence of both proteins within the cytosolic plasma membrane of resting T cells.
source: Co-association of PTPN22 and CSK results in residence of both proteins within the cytosolic plasma membrane of resting T cells through the association of CSK with another TCR inhibitory protein, PAG (Davidson et al., 2016; Simoncelli et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Davidson et al., 2016 and Simoncelli et al., 2020.

claim: The R620W substitution in PTPN22 is located within a proline rich, C-terminal domain.
source: The R620W substitution in PTPN22 is located within a proline rich, C-terminal domain and reduces the interaction of PTPN22 with CSK leading to altered localization of PTPN22 (Bottini et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bottini et al., 2004.

claim: The R620W substitution reduces the interaction of PTPN22 with CSK leading to altered localization of PTPN22.
source: The R620W substitution in PTPN22 is located within a proline rich, C-terminal domain and reduces the interaction of PTPN22 with CSK leading to altered localization of PTPN22 (Bottini et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bottini et al., 2004.

claim: Primary T cells isolated from carriers of the PTPN22 risk variant display significantly weaker responses to TCR engagement.
source: Primary T cells isolated from carriers of the PTPN22 risk variant display significantly weaker responses to TCR engagement, as measured by calcium flux, cytokine release, and other metrics (Rieck et al., 2007; Vang et al., 2005; Arechiga et al., 2009; Vang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Rieck et al., 2007; Vang et al., 2005; Arechiga et al., 2009; Vang et al., 2013.

claim: In murine models, expression of the PTPN22 risk variant leads to enhanced TCR responses.
source: However, in murine models, expression of the risk variant leads to enhanced TCR responses, as measured by the same metrics in addition to increased T cell proliferation and survival (Zhang et al., 2011; Dai et al., 2013; Lin et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2011; Dai et al., 2013; Lin et al., 2016.

claim: Genetic ablation of PTPN22 in both mouse and human primary T cells results in enhanced TCR signaling relative to PTPN22 wild type cells.
source: In contrast, genetic ablation of PTPN22 in both mouse and human primary T cells results in enhanced TCR signaling relative to PTPN22 wild type cells; findings similar to murine risk model yet opposite of the phenotypes described in human carriers of the risk variant (Hasegawa et al., 2004; Anderson et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hasegawa et al., 2004 and Anderson et al., 2019.

claim: Genetic ablation of ptpn22 in a fixed TCR murine model showed that loss of PTPN22 preferentially impacts T cells responses to low-avidity antigens, but not high-avidity antigens.
source: Furthermore, genetic ablation of ptpn22 in a fixed TCR murine model has shown that loss of PTPN22 preferentially impacts T cells responses to low-avidity antigens, but not high-avidity antigens (Salmond et al., 2014); driving increased proliferation and skewing toward a Th1 phenotype in ptpn22 KO T cells.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Salmond et al., 2014.

claim: Loss of ptpn22 drives increased proliferation and skewing toward a Th1 phenotype in ptpn22 KO T cells in a fixed TCR murine model.
source: Furthermore, genetic ablation of ptpn22 in a fixed TCR murine model has shown that loss of PTPN22 preferentially impacts T cells responses to low-avidity antigens, but not high-avidity antigens (Salmond et al., 2014); driving increased proliferation and skewing toward a Th1 phenotype in ptpn22 KO T cells.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Salmond et al., 2014.

claim: The PTPN22 risk variant is associated with an increase in memory lymphocyte populations.
source: For instance, the risk variant is associated with an increase in memory lymphocyte populations and expanded pro-inflammatory/Th1 T cells and both exhibit increased risk of autoimmune manifestations (Vang et al., 2013; Dai et al., 2013; Sanchez-Blanco et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Vang et al., 2013; Dai et al., 2013; Sanchez-Blanco et al., 2018.

claim: The PTPN22 risk variant is associated with expanded pro-inflammatory/Th1 T cells.
source: For instance, the risk variant is associated with an increase in memory lymphocyte populations and expanded pro-inflammatory/Th1 T cells and both exhibit increased risk of autoimmune manifestations (Vang et al., 2013; Dai et al., 2013; Sanchez-Blanco et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Vang et al., 2013; Dai et al., 2013; Sanchez-Blanco et al., 2018.

claim: A 120 bp ssODN design with a long 5' homology arm (ssODN V3, 5' arm 89 bp/3' arm 29 bp) efficiently introduced the desired coding sequence alterations in adult peripheral blood CD4 T cells.
source: We found that in adult peripheral blood CD4 T cells, a 120 bp ssODN design with a long 5' homology arm (ssODN V3, 5' arm 89 bp/3' arm 29 bp) efficiently introduced the desired coding sequence alterations (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), in line with previous findings (Richardson et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and citation to Richardson et al., 2016.

claim: PTPN22 non-risk and risk edited populations exhibited average HDR rates of ~50%.
source: Both edited populations exhibited average HDR rates of ~50%, and no detectable editing was present in mock edited populations.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: No detectable editing was present in mock edited populations.
source: Both edited populations exhibited average HDR rates of ~50%, and no detectable editing was present in mock edited populations.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: PTPN22 non-risk and risk edited populations retained equivalent expression levels of PTPN22.
source: Western blot analysis confirmed that, PTPN22 non-risk and risk edited populations retained equivalent expression levels of PTPN22 (with a reduction in total PTPN22 protein compared with mock edited cells reflecting the NHEJ-mediated loss of protein expression in the absence of successful HDR).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D-E.

claim: PTPN22 KO populations exhibited near total absence of protein expression.
source: As expected, PTPN22 KO populations exhibited near total absence of protein expression (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D-E.

claim: Wild type PTPN22 alleles were nearly undetectable in edited populations (<1% of total alleles).
source: Wild type PTPN22 alleles were nearly undetectable in edited populations (<1% of total alleles), indicating that resulting genotypes of edited T cells can be assumed to a mixture of biallelic HDR, biallelic NHEJ (PTPN22 KO), or HDR and NHEJ on opposite alleles (hemizygous).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from ddPCR analysis.

claim: Mock edited cells had significantly less expression of the activation markers CD69, CD25, and CD71 compared with gene edited populations.
source: As all PTPN22 edits produced some loss of PTPN22 expression, and PTPN22 is responsible for restraining TCR activation, it was unsurprising to find that mock edited cells had significantly less expression of the activation markers CD69, CD25, and CD71 compared with gene edited populations (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: PTPN22 KO populations expressed the highest levels of activation markers CD69, CD25, and CD71.
source: However, it was striking that, while PTPN22 KO populations expressed the highest levels of these activation markers, the PTPN22 risk edited cells, in comparison with non-risk edited cells, also exhibited increased expression of CD25 and CD71 at 48 hr post stimulation and a trend toward increased CD69 expression as early as 6 hr post stimulation (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: PTPN22 risk edited cells exhibited increased expression of CD25 and CD71 at 48 hr post stimulation compared with non-risk edited cells.
source: However, it was striking that, while PTPN22 KO populations expressed the highest levels of these activation markers, the PTPN22 risk edited cells, in comparison with non-risk edited cells, also exhibited increased expression of CD25 and CD71 at 48 hr post stimulation and a trend toward increased CD69 expression as early as 6 hr post stimulation (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: PTPN22 risk edited cells showed a trend toward increased CD69 expression as early as 6 hr post stimulation compared with non-risk edited cells.
source: However, it was striking that, while PTPN22 KO populations expressed the highest levels of these activation markers, the PTPN22 risk edited cells, in comparison with non-risk edited cells, also exhibited increased expression of CD25 and CD71 at 48 hr post stimulation and a trend toward increased CD69 expression as early as 6 hr post stimulation (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: TCR signaling strength is increased in cells expressing the PTPN22 risk variant.
source: Together, this data strongly suggests that TCR signaling strength is increased in cells expressing the PTPN22 risk variant, and, that this phenotype is most similar to PTPN22 KO T cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The phenotype of PTPN22 risk variant cells is most similar to PTPN22 KO T cells.
source: Together, this data strongly suggests that TCR signaling strength is increased in cells expressing the PTPN22 risk variant, and, that this phenotype is most similar to PTPN22 KO T cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: No differences in the number of cells producing IFNγ or IL-2 were observed based upon edits made to PTPN22 in Th1 skewing conditions.
source: Three days after stimulation we found most cells producing Th1 associated cytokines, however no differences in the number of cells producing IFNγ or IL-2 were observed based upon edits made to PTPN22 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: Addition of LV transduction prior to gene editing did not impact gene editing outcomes or rates of HDR.
source: Addition of LV transduction prior to gene editing did not impact gene editing outcomes or rates of HDR (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The two TCRs (L-TCR and H-TCR) triggered different rates of proliferation over 3 days, consistent with their reported avidity.
source: Following stimulation of TCR+ cord blood T cells with peptide loaded APCs, the alternative self-reactive TCRs responded to IGRP peptide at markedly different magnitudes. The two TCRs, that we term: 'lower avidity TCR' or L-TCR, and 'higher avidity TCR' or H-TCR, triggered different rates of proliferation over 3 days (based on either dye dilution or direct cell counts), consistent with their reported avidity (Figure 3C and D; Linsley et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and D and citation to Linsley et al., 2021.

claim: L-TCR+ PTPN22 KO cells had significantly increased proliferation relative to mock edited L-TCR cells across a range of peptide doses.
source: Notably, upon combining antigen specific stimulation with PTPN22 KO gene editing, we found that L-TCR+ PTPN22 KO cells had significantly increased proliferation relative to mock edited L-TCR cells across a range of peptide doses (Figure 3C–E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C-E.

claim: H-TCR+ expressing edited T cells showed similar proliferation rates in response to multiple antigen doses, regardless of PTPN22 genotype.
source: In contrast, H-TCR + expressing edited T cells showed similar proliferation rates in response to multiple antigen doses, regardless of PTPN22 genotype (Figure 3D and F; Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D, F, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: In cells expressing L-TCR, the loss of PTPN22 resulted in significantly greater proportion of phosphorylated S6 kinase positive cells.
source: In cells expressing L-TCR, the loss of PTPN22 resulted in significantly greater proportion of phosphorylated S6 kinase positive cells, while cells expressing H-TCR, PTPN22 KO showed no impact on the relative percentage of pS6+ cells (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: In cells expressing H-TCR, PTPN22 KO showed no impact on the relative percentage of pS6+ cells.
source: In cells expressing L-TCR, the loss of PTPN22 resulted in significantly greater proportion of phosphorylated S6 kinase positive cells, while cells expressing H-TCR, PTPN22 KO showed no impact on the relative percentage of pS6+ cells (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: L-TCR expressing PTPN22 KO T cells expressed higher levels of activation markers including CD69, CD25, and CD71 compared to mock edited T cells.
source: Two days post peptide stimulation, L-TCR expressing PTPN22 KO T cells, in comparison to mock edited T cells from the same cord blood donor also expressing L-TCR, expressed higher levels of activation markers including CD69, CD25, and CD71 (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: H-TCR expressing PTPN22 KO T cells exhibited no differences in activation marker expression in comparison to control T cells.
source: In contrast, H-TCR expressing PTPN22 KO T cells exhibited no differences in comparison to control T cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Loss of PTPN22 activity preferentially permits enhanced signaling in response to low-avidity TCR engagement in primary human T cells.
source: Together, these results demonstrate that loss of PTPN22 activity preferentially permits enhanced signaling in response to low-avidity TCR engagement in primary human T cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: H-TCR+ PTPN22 KO T cells exhibited no difference in frequency of IFNγ or IL-2 producing cells relative to mock edited cells.
source: H-TCR+ PTPN22 KO T cells exhibited no difference in frequency of IFNγ or IL-2 producing cells relative to mock edited cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: The proportion of L-TCR+ cells that generated IFNγ were increased by loss of PTPN22.
source: In contrast, the proportion of L-TCR+ cells that generated IFNγ were increased by loss of PTPN22 and risk edited cells exhibited a similar trend though not significant (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: PTPN22 risk edited cells contained a significantly higher proportion of IL-2 producing cells.
source: Notably, PTPN22 risk edited cells contained a significantly higher proportion of IL-2 producing cells (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: gDNA based ddPCR analysis on FAC sorted TCR+ cells prior to stimulation demonstrated equal proportions of PTPN22 risk and non-risk edited alleles.
source: gDNA based ddPCR analysis on FAC sorted TCR+ cells prior to stimulation demonstrated equal proportions of PTPN22 risk and non-risk edited alleles (Figure 6B–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B-C.

claim: ddPCR revealed nearly twice as many PTPN22 risk edited over non-risk edited alleles within the proliferating cell population after peptide stimulation.
source: ddPCR revealed nearly twice as many PTPN22 risk edited over non-risk edited alleles within the proliferating cell population (Figure 6B–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B-C.

claim: Human T cells expressing the PTPN22 risk variant exhibit increased proliferation in response to low-avidity TCR engagement.
source: Together, this data supports a hypothesized model (Figure 6A) wherein human T cells expressing the PTPN22 risk variant exhibit increased proliferation in response to low-avidity TCR engagement.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: gDNA taken from stimulated but non-proliferating TCR+ cells showed a partial increase in PTPN22 risk edited alleles relative to input.
source: Interestingly, gDNA taken from stimulated but non-proliferating TCR+ cells also showed a partial increase in PTPN22 risk edited alleles relative to input.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: Increased TCR signal strength in risk variant T cells may promote enhanced cell survival.
source: While this difference was less robust than among proliferating cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–B), it suggests that increased TCR signal strength in risk variant T cells may promote enhanced cell survival, a finding that will require additional study.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: PTPN22 risk variant expressing T cells exhibit a phenotype similar to PTPN22 KO T cells, leading to increased expression of TCR induced activation responses markers.
source: Notably, our data clearly demonstrate that PTPN22 risk variant expressing T cells exhibit a phenotype similar to PTPN22 KO T cells, leading to increased expression of TCR induced activation responses markers.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from Figures 2-6.

claim: PTPN22 deficiency predominantly impacts T cells activated in response to low-avidity TCR engagement.
source: Further, using transgenic TCR delivery and cognate peptide-mediated activation, in tandem with our gene editing platform, we show that PTPN22 deficiency predominantly impacts T cells activated in response to low-avidity TCR engagement.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from Figures 3-6.

claim: PTPN22 function is largely dispensable in T cells receiving a high-avidity TCR signal.
source: In contrast, PTPN22 function is largely dispensable in T cells receiving a high-avidity TCR signal.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from Figures 3-4.

claim: The PTPN22 risk variant may contribute to autoimmune responses by selectively expanding the pool of lower avidity, self-reactive T cells.
source: Together, these data suggest that the PTPN22 risk variant may contribute to autoimmune responses, at least in part, by selectively expanding the pool of lower avidity, self-reactive T cells and skewing such cells toward a pro-inflammatory phenotype.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The PTPN22 risk variant may contribute to autoimmune responses by skewing lower avidity, self-reactive T cells toward a pro-inflammatory phenotype.
source: Together, these data suggest that the PTPN22 risk variant may contribute to autoimmune responses, at least in part, by selectively expanding the pool of lower avidity, self-reactive T cells and skewing such cells toward a pro-inflammatory phenotype.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The findings are consistent with previous work in a fixed TCR murine model that found loss of ptpn22 to preferentially impact low-avidity TCR stimulation.
source: Our findings are consistent with previous work in a fixed TCR murine model that also found loss of ptpn22 to preferentially impact low-avidity TCR stimulation (Salmond et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a comparison of the current findings with previous work cited.

claim: The editing platform utilizes a designer nuclease that generates a dsDNA break in close proximity to the target site for HDR editing.
source: Our editing platform utilizes a designer nuclease that generates a dsDNA break in close proximity to the target site for HDR editing.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: The editing platform allows for generation of edited cells with high rates of HDR.
source: This combined approach allows for: (a) generation of edited cells with high rates of HDR; (b) equivalent HDR rates for alternative coding changes within the target gene via use of a series of ssODN donors; and (c) achieving editing outcomes while controlling for the overall HDR/NHEJ ratio.
evidence: This describes the advantages of the methodology used in the study.

claim: The editing platform allows for equivalent HDR rates for alternative coding changes within the target gene via use of a series of ssODN donors.
source: This combined approach allows for: (a) generation of edited cells with high rates of HDR; (b) equivalent HDR rates for alternative coding changes within the target gene via use of a series of ssODN donors; and (c) achieving editing outcomes while controlling for the overall HDR/NHEJ ratio.
evidence: This describes the advantages of the methodology used in the study.

claim: The editing platform allows for achieving editing outcomes while controlling for the overall HDR/NHEJ ratio.
source: This combined approach allows for: (a) generation of edited cells with high rates of HDR; (b) equivalent HDR rates for alternative coding changes within the target gene via use of a series of ssODN donors; and (c) achieving editing outcomes while controlling for the overall HDR/NHEJ ratio.
evidence: This describes the advantages of the methodology used in the study.

claim: Expression of the PTPN22 risk variant can increase proliferation of primary human T cells expressing a low-avidity TCR.
source: We demonstrate that expression of the PTPN22 risk variant can increase proliferation of primary human T cells expressing a low-avidity TCR, findings that mimic PTPN22 KO T cells.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from Figure 6.

claim: Loss of PTPN22 regulation promotes the development of a pro-inflammatory phenotype in T cells using a low-avidity TCR.
source: Furthermore, we show that loss of PTPN22 regulation promotes the development of a pro-inflammatory phenotype in T cells using a low-avidity TCR.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from Figure 5.

claim: Both humans and mice with the PTPN22 risk variant exhibit expanded memory T cell and Th1 populations.
source: Indeed, while previous human data and mouse models have led to contradictory conclusions regarding the impact of the risk variant on proximal TCR signaling, both humans and mice with the PTPN22 risk variant exhibit expanded memory T cell and Th1 populations (Rieck et al., 2007; Vang et al., 2013; Dai et al., 2013; Salmond et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Rieck et al., 2007; Vang et al., 2013; Dai et al., 2013; Salmond et al., 2014.

claim: PTPN22 is expressed in multiple immune and hematopoietic subsets and has multiple functions.
source: Importantly, PTPN22 is expressed in multiple immune and hematopoietic subsets and has been shown to have multiple functions (Rawlings et al., 2015; Stanford and Bottini, 2014; Armitage et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Rawlings et al., 2015; Stanford and Bottini, 2014; Armitage et al., 2021.

claim: Gene edited cells exhibited proximal phosphorylation changes in response to antibody-based stimulation.
source: While gene edited cells exhibited proximal phosphorylation changes in response to antibody-based stimulation, biochemical changes were not detected until 24 hr post peptide-based stimulation.
evidence: This describes a limitation of the methodology used in the study.

claim: Biochemical changes were not detected until 24 hr post peptide-based stimulation.
source: While gene edited cells exhibited proximal phosphorylation changes in response to antibody-based stimulation, biochemical changes were not detected until 24 hr post peptide-based stimulation.
evidence: This describes a limitation of the methodology used in the study.

claim: The findings provide an important bridge between inconsistencies connecting PTPN22 to autoimmune risk in previous mouse vs. primary human cell data.
source: Also, while our findings provide an important bridge between inconsistencies connecting PTPN22 to autoimmune risk in previous mouse vs. primary human cell data, it should not be viewed as a replacement for mouse models.
